The gold's javadoc promises the explicit name a JsonProperty annotation gives to an enumeration value, which for EnumWithPropertyAnno.B is "b", not null. No change of the argument above the gold helps: every Enum a caller can hand on for B (the value, the constant found through getDeclaringClass().getEnumConstants() or ClassUtil.findEnumType(..).getEnumConstants(), Enum.valueOf) is the same object of the anonymous subclass; a different fallback at hop 1 (toString()) gives "bb". The convention is pinned outside the gold: ClassUtil.findEnumType(Enum<?>) (the formal enumeration type is the class of the instance for simple enumerations and its superclass for enums with instance fields or methods; 'enums with body are sub-classes of the formal type', the same getSuperclass() != Enum.class step) and EnumValues.constructFromName ('Enum types with per-instance sub-classes need special handling', via ClassUtil.findEnumType) with TestClassUtil testFindEnumType and the subclassed-enum serialization and deserialization tests passing.
